builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Autonomous intelligence for mining productivity: a multi-agent AI approach to operational value creation
summary: EI2ROC proposes a three-tier multi-agent architecture (LLM orchestrator plus specialised monitoring and production-capacity agents over an MCP-style tool interface) intended to replace manual, siloed supervision in mining Integrated Remote Operation Centres, alongside a six-dimension benchmarking framework for industrial agentic systems. It costs orchestration complexity, LLM inference cost and latency per decision in a safety-critical setting, and the paper itself marks most components as reference design or future work, with only preliminary cost and latency observations from one site. It can fail through orchestrator errors propagating to SCADA-connected actions, unmet real-time and regulatory-auditability requirements, and the absence of validated benchmarks for the industrial blind spot the paper identifies.
rationale: The paper is a domain-specific architectural blueprint with an implemented prototype but no quantified gains, so it is relevant context for agentic orchestration and evaluation design but not something to adopt or benchmark on a constrained production stack.
technique: Multi-agent LLM architecture for mining operation centres
